item.text: {"rubric":[{"claim_id":"c1","claim_type":"core","weight":15,"statement":"`Adapter.format` treats a `dspy.History` input specially: it looks for an input field whose annotation is exactly `History` and only takes the conversation-history path when that field exists.","span_ids":["s1","s2"]},{"claim_id":"c2","claim_type":"core","weight":25,"statement":"When a history field is present, DSPy removes it from the signature with `signature.delete(history_field_name)` and deletes it from `inputs`, so the history object itself is not left to be serialized into the live current-turn payload.","span_ids":["s2","s3"]},{"claim_id":"c3","claim_type":"core","weight":30,"statement":"`format_conversation_history` expands `inputs[history_field_name].messages` into real earlier chat turns by appending one `user` message and one `assistant` message for each saved exchange.","span_ids":["s3","s4"]},{"claim_id":"c4","claim_type":"core","weight":20,"statement":"After the reconstructed history turns, `Adapter.format` appends the current invocation as a fresh final `user` message rather than folding it into the prior history.","span_ids":["s2","s4"]},{"claim_id":"c5","claim_type":"supporting","weight":10,"statement":"The outbound message list still starts with a system message built from the original signature, and the regression test shows one saved exchange being sent as `system`, prior `user`, prior `assistant`, then current `user`.","span_ids":["s2","s4"]}],"evidence":[{"span_id":"s1","path":"dspy/adapters/base.py","start_line":458,"end_line":462},{"span_id":"s2","path":"dspy/adapters/base.py","start_line":267,"end_line":293},{"span_id":"s3","path":"dspy/adapters/base.py","start_line":498,"end_line":521},{"span_id":"s4","path":"tests/predict/test_predict.py","start_line":711,"end_line":724}]}
